nodes.Name: benchmarkLock
nodes.DocComment: Global lock to ensure only one benchmark runs at a time.

nodes.Name: memStats
nodes.DocComment: Used for every benchmark for measuring memory.

nodes.Name: InternalBenchmark
nodes.DocComment:
InternalBenchmark is an internal type but exported because it is cross-package;
it is part of the implementation of the "go test" command.

nodes.Name: B
nodes.DocComment:
B is a type passed to [Benchmark] functions to manage benchmark
timing and control the number of iterations.

A benchmark ends when its Benchmark function returns or calls any of the methods
[B.FailNow], [B.Fatal], [B.Fatalf], [B.SkipNow], [B.Skip], or [B.Skipf].
Those methods must be called only from the goroutine running the Benchmark function.
The other reporting methods, such as the variations of [B.Log] and [B.Error],
may be called simultaneously from multiple goroutines.

Like in tests, benchmark logs are accumulated during execution
and dumped to standard output when done. Unlike in tests, benchmark logs
are always printed, so as not to hide output whose existence may be
affecting benchmark results.

Fields.Name: importPath
Fields.DocComment: import path of the package containing the benchmark

Fields.Name: previousN
Fields.DocComment: number of iterations in the previous run

Fields.Name: previousDuration
Fields.DocComment: total duration of the previous run

Fields.Name: missingBytes
Fields.DocComment: one of the subbenchmarks does not have bytes set.

nodes.Name: StartTimer
nodes.DocComment:
StartTimer starts timing a test. This function is called automatically
before a benchmark starts, but it can also be used to resume timing after
a call to [B.StopTimer].

nodes.Name: StopTimer
nodes.DocComment:
StopTimer stops timing a test. This can be used to pause the timer
while performing steps that you don't want to measure.

nodes.Name: ResetTimer
nodes.DocComment:
ResetTimer zeroes the elapsed benchmark time and memory allocation counters
and deletes user-reported metrics.
It does not affect whether the timer is running.

nodes.Name: SetBytes
nodes.DocComment:
SetBytes records the number of bytes processed in a single operation.
If this is called, the benchmark will report ns/op and MB/s.

nodes.Name: ReportAllocs
nodes.DocComment:
ReportAllocs enables malloc statistics for this benchmark.
It is equivalent to setting -test.benchmem, but it only affects the
benchmark function that calls ReportAllocs.

nodes.Name: runN
nodes.DocComment: runN runs a single benchmark for the specified number of iterations.

nodes.Name: run1
nodes.DocComment:
run1 runs the first iteration of benchFunc. It reports whether more
iterations of this benchmarks should be run.

nodes.Name: run
nodes.DocComment:
run executes the benchmark in a separate goroutine, including all of its
subbenchmarks. b must not have subbenchmarks.

nodes.Name: maxBenchPredictIters
nodes.DocComment: Don't run more than 1e9 times. (This also keeps n in int range on 32 bit platforms.)

nodes.Name: launch
nodes.DocComment:
launch launches the benchmark function. It gradually increases the number
of benchmark iterations until the benchmark runs for the requested benchtime.
launch is run by the doBench function as a separate goroutine.
run1 must have been called on b.

nodes.Name: Elapsed
nodes.DocComment:
Elapsed returns the measured elapsed time of the benchmark.
The duration reported by Elapsed matches the one measured by
[B.StartTimer], [B.StopTimer], and [B.ResetTimer].

nodes.Name: ReportMetric
nodes.DocComment:
ReportMetric adds "n unit" to the reported benchmark results.
If the metric is per-iteration, the caller should divide by b.N,
and by convention units should end in "/op".
ReportMetric overrides any previously reported value for the same unit.
ReportMetric panics if unit is the empty string or if unit contains
any whitespace.
If unit is a unit normally reported by the benchmark framework itself
(such as "allocs/op"), ReportMetric will override that metric.
Setting "ns/op" to 0 will suppress that built-in metric.

nodes.Name: Loop
nodes.DocComment:
Loop returns true as long as the benchmark should continue running.

A typical benchmark is structured like:

	func Benchmark(b *testing.B) {
		... setup ...
		for b.Loop() {
			... code to measure ...
		}
		... cleanup ...
	}

Loop resets the benchmark timer the first time it is called in a benchmark,
so any setup performed prior to starting the benchmark loop does not count
toward the benchmark measurement. Likewise, when it returns false, it stops
the timer so cleanup code is not measured.

Within the body of a "for b.Loop() { ... }" loop, arguments to and
results from function calls and assigned variables within the loop are kept
alive, preventing the compiler from fully optimizing away the loop body.
Currently, this is implemented as a compiler transformation that wraps such
variables with a runtime.KeepAlive intrinsic call. This applies only to
statements syntactically between the curly braces of the loop, and the loop
condition must be written exactly as "b.Loop()".

After Loop returns false, b.N contains the total number of iterations that
ran, so the benchmark may use b.N to compute other average metrics.

Prior to the introduction of Loop, benchmarks were expected to contain an
explicit loop from 0 to b.N. Benchmarks should either use Loop or contain a
loop to b.N, but not both. Loop offers more automatic management of the
benchmark timer, and runs each benchmark function only once per measurement,
whereas b.N-based benchmarks must run the benchmark function (and any
associated setup and cleanup) several times.

nodes.Name: loopPoisonTimer
nodes.DocComment:
The loopPoison constants can be OR'd into B.loop.i to cause it to fall back
to the slow path.

nodes.Name: loopPoisonMask
nodes.DocComment:
The loopPoison constants can be OR'd into B.loop.i to cause it to fall back
to the slow path.

nodes.Name: BenchmarkResult
nodes.DocComment: BenchmarkResult contains the results of a benchmark run.

Fields.Name: MemAllocs
Fields.DocComment: The total number of memory allocations.

Fields.Name: MemBytes
Fields.DocComment: The total number of bytes allocated.

nodes.Name: NsPerOp
nodes.DocComment: NsPerOp returns the "ns/op" metric.

nodes.Name: mbPerSec
nodes.DocComment: mbPerSec returns the "MB/s" metric.

nodes.Name: AllocsPerOp
nodes.DocComment:
AllocsPerOp returns the "allocs/op" metric,
which is calculated as r.MemAllocs / r.N.

nodes.Name: AllocedBytesPerOp
nodes.DocComment:
AllocedBytesPerOp returns the "B/op" metric,
which is calculated as r.MemBytes / r.N.

nodes.Name: String
nodes.DocComment:
String returns a summary of the benchmark results.
It follows the benchmark result line format from
https://golang.org/design/14313-benchmark-format, not including the
benchmark name.
Extra metrics override built-in metrics of the same name.
String does not include allocs/op or B/op, since those are reported
by [BenchmarkResult.MemString].

nodes.Name: MemString
nodes.DocComment: MemString returns r.AllocedBytesPerOp and r.AllocsPerOp in the same format as 'go test'.

nodes.Name: benchmarkName
nodes.DocComment: benchmarkName returns full name of benchmark including procs suffix.

nodes.Name: RunBenchmarks
nodes.DocComment:
RunBenchmarks is an internal function but exported because it is cross-package;
it is part of the implementation of the "go test" command.

nodes.Name: processBench
nodes.DocComment: processBench runs bench b for the configured CPU counts and prints the results.

nodes.Name: hideStdoutForTesting
nodes.DocComment:
If hideStdoutForTesting is true, Run does not print the benchName.
This avoids a spurious print during 'go test' on package testing itself,
which invokes b.Run in its own tests (see sub_test.go).

nodes.Name: Run
nodes.DocComment:
Run benchmarks f as a subbenchmark with the given name. It reports
whether there were any failures.

A subbenchmark is like any other benchmark. A benchmark that calls Run at
least once will not be measured itself and will be called once with N=1.

nodes.Name: add
nodes.DocComment:
add simulates running benchmarks in sequence in a single iteration. It is
used to give some meaningful results in case func Benchmark is used in
combination with Run.

nodes.Name: trimOutput
nodes.DocComment: trimOutput shortens the output from a benchmark, which can be very long.

nodes.Name: PB
nodes.DocComment: A PB is used by RunParallel for running parallel benchmarks.

Fields.Name: globalN
Fields.DocComment: shared between all worker goroutines iteration counter

Fields.Name: grain
Fields.DocComment: acquire that many iterations from globalN at once

Fields.Name: bN
Fields.DocComment: total number of iterations to execute (b.N)

nodes.Name: Next
nodes.DocComment: Next reports whether there are more iterations to execute.

nodes.Name: RunParallel
nodes.DocComment:
RunParallel runs a benchmark in parallel.
It creates multiple goroutines and distributes b.N iterations among them.
The number of goroutines defaults to GOMAXPROCS. To increase parallelism for
non-CPU-bound benchmarks, call [B.SetParallelism] before RunParallel.
RunParallel is usually used with the go test -cpu flag.

The body function will be run in each goroutine. It should set up any
goroutine-local state and then iterate until pb.Next returns false.
It should not use the [B.StartTimer], [B.StopTimer], or [B.ResetTimer] functions,
because they have global effect. It should also not call [B.Run].

RunParallel reports ns/op values as wall time for the benchmark as a whole,
not the sum of wall time or CPU time over each parallel goroutine.

nodes.Name: SetParallelism
nodes.DocComment:
SetParallelism sets the number of goroutines used by [B.RunParallel] to p*GOMAXPROCS.
There is usually no need to call SetParallelism for CPU-bound benchmarks.
If p is less than 1, this call will have no effect.

nodes.Name: Benchmark
nodes.DocComment:
Benchmark benchmarks a single function. It is useful for creating
custom benchmarks that do not use the "go test" command.

If f depends on testing flags, then [Init] must be used to register
those flags before calling Benchmark and before calling [flag.Parse].

If f calls Run, the result will be an estimate of running all its
subbenchmarks that don't call Run in sequence in a single benchmark.
